newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, C.America to set $200M development funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, C.America to set $200M development funds.

text.p: Taiwan's top economic policymaker said on Tuesday the government and its central American allies have decided to set up a US$200 million fund to help economic development in Central America.

"We plan to set up an economic and trade fund with each side offering US$100 million over a 10-year span to help economic development in Central America," Chiang Pin-kung, chairman of the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development, told a news conference.
The fund was jointly established by Taiwan and its five allies in Central America -- Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua.
The five Central American nations on Tuesday opened a joint trade office in Taipei to promote bilateral trade and investment.

Officials from the five nations said their diplomatic relations with Taiwan would remain unchanged even though their Hong Kong consulates had been forced to close or downgrade because of Hong Kong's July 1 return to Chinese sovereignty.
China, rivals with Taiwan since a civil war split them in 1949, regards the exiled Republic of China government as a renegade province that one day must be reunified under mainland sovereignty.
Communist China insists the Nationalist-ruled island is not eligible to join major international organisations and warns other countries against forging ties with the island.
Most of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies are underdeveloped states in Africa and central America.
Taiwan and China have competed aggressively for diplomatic recognition since 1949, often accusing each other of using large sums of cash and aid to woo potential backers.
